freeze_statement: Re-freeze after the author's directive that Figures 1 and 2 ship as editable Visio OLE objects in the Word deliverable. ONE tracked file moves - papers/DT-GSK.docx - and nothing else: the PDF, the supplement in both formats, the cover letter, main.tex and all three CSVs are byte-identical to the pass-36 mint. No number, rank, p-value, test, standing or registered outcome changes; the figures are the same drawings, now double-click-editable. This reverses the D-0042 decision to keep the fold-in opt-in, and the reversal is substantively right rather than merely directed: two of the three reasons given there did not survive measurement. The size cost is +9,869 bytes, about 1 percent, not a material enlargement; and the 'an editor without Visio meets an object they cannot open' risk is void because each w:object retains its PNG preview, so the figures render exactly as before without Visio. Only the third reason stands - MDPI asks for figures as a separate 600 dpi ZIP, which is built and shipped - and that is not a reason to withhold editability from the DOCX. Also corrected while enabling it: the opt-in block regenerated the tracked flowchart_*.vsdx on every build, rewriting validated artifacts as a side effect; they are now regenerated only when absent and were confirmed untouched across two builds. validate_visio_ole.py now covers the SHIPPED DT-GSK.docx rather than only the standalone variant, checking on every run that both embedded drawings are byte-identical to their tracked sources, that both use the 'package' relationship type (the defect that made Word render them as flat images, fixed in D-0041 and author-confirmed in D-0042), and that each embedded copy re-validates independently. Verification: DOCX byte-identical across two consecutive builds at the pinned epoch 1783641600; 2 OLE objects with 2 previews retained; validate_docx passes on both documents; cross-format parity, doc-consistency, artifact labels and build hygiene all green.
